Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroDef Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroDef Technologies' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and David Chen, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those statements.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AeroDef Technologies delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense systems, space and mission systems, and commercial aerospace. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, I'll highlight our key areas of focus: overall company performance highlights and key takeaways; backlog growth; updates on key programs; geopolitical factors influencing defense spending; updated revenue and earnings guidance for the full year; and free cash flow generation and utilization.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to position us for leadership in next-generation air dominance. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including contributions to the F-35 Lightning II and hypersonic weapons, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with robust aftermarket services.

Let me start with overall performance highlights. In Q3, we achieved record revenue of $2.78 billion, up 14% year-over-year and beating our guidance midpoint by $80 million. Adjusted EPS was $2.12, a 22% increase from $1.74 last year, powered by strong execution, favorable mix, and cost discipline. Free cash flow hit $450 million, up 30% YoY, strengthening our balance sheet to $1.2 billion in net cash and funding $250 million in share repurchases. Defense, our bedrock at 62% of revenue, reached $1.72 billion, up 18%, driven by F-35 milestones like 1,200 cumulative shipsets and hypersonic ramps for ARRW. Book-to-bill was 1.35x, with total backlog at $48.7 billion, including $12.4 billion funded. Key wins included a $2.1 billion IDIQ for next-gen C4ISR and $850 million for directed energy prototypes under HELIOS. Margins expanded 120 basis points to 13.8% via digital thread efficiencies cutting touch labor 15%.

Commercial aviation at 28% or $780 million grew 9% despite supply chain issues, with nacelle deliveries for 737 MAX and A320neo up 22% to 450 units. Aftermarket surged 25% to $220 million, boosted by AI/ML predictive analytics achieving 98% engine health accuracy, slashing downtime 20% for airlines like Delta and United. Space and advanced systems at 10% or $280 million jumped 25%, with Starship propulsion modules and a $1.2 billion NASA Artemis avionics contract. Margins rose to 11.2% from additive manufacturing shortening thruster lead times 40%.

Enterprise margins hit 12.6%, up 90 basis points, with $180 million in year-to-date Lean Sigma savings targeting $250 million for FY24. R&D up 12% to $210 million or 7.6% of sales focuses on UAS, NGAD enablers, and hybrid-electric propulsion.

Geopolitically, U.S. DoD FY25 requests at $850 billion up 4.1% align our hypersonics and SM-6 with Pacific Deterrence. Europe sales up 28% to $420 million on F-35 for Tempest and Patriot for Poland. Asia-Pacific up 35% to $310 million via AUKUS subs and Japan's GCAP. Middle East up 15% to $180 million on Saudi drone defense.

Our backlog grew to $178.2 billion, up $26.8 billion or 18% YoY and $12.4 billion or 7.5% QoQ—eighth straight double-digit quarter. Aeronautics at $74.9 billion up 23% on $8.1 billion F-35 Lot 17 and $2.3 billion NGAD. Missiles at $52.6 billion up 18% with $4.2 billion hypersonics. Space $28.7 billion up 13% on GPS IIIF and Vulcan. Rotary $22.0 billion up 10% on CH-53K and MH-60R. U.S. 72% at $128.3 billion up 20%, international up 25% to $35.4 billion.

On programs, NGAD hit CDR for fighter and CCA, XA-102 engine 15% better SFC, 14 air vehicles in LRIP. F-35 Lot 17 at 156 aircraft, Block 4C certified. ARRW/HACM flight test #5 success, 28 rounds delivered. Orion CV2 on track, Golden Dome IOC with 42 sats. MQ-9B at 18 airframes.

John will expand on guidance and financials, Maria on operations, and Elena on technology.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Alex. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $2.78 billion, a 14% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted earnings per share were $2.12. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $1.2 billion in net cash. Our guidance for the full year is now at the high end.

Good morning, everyone. Before turning back to Alex, let me walk through our updated full-year 2024 guidance, reflecting strong momentum across our portfolio amid dynamic geopolitics and commercial recovery. Our segments are Defense Systems with F-35, hypersonics; Space & Mission with satellites, launches, C4ISR; Commercial with MRO, composites for Boeing and Airbus.

Initial guidance was $28.5-29.5 billion revenue, $12.50-13.50 adjusted EPS, 11.0-11.5% margins. Today, raising midpoint: revenue $29.2-30.2 billion, up 4%. Defense to $18.8-19.5 billion, up 6%, from F-35 Lot 15 ramp, TR-3 Block 4 at 15% higher sorties, $2.1 billion LRIP, $450 million FMS Israel/Japan; JASSM-ER/hypersonics at 110% capacity, $1.2 billion IDIQ, 28% YoY bookings; $300 million DARPA HAWC/CCA.

Space $6.5-6.8 billion, flat but visible: three Vulcan H2 launches, SDA Tranche 2 75% funded, $800 million AUKUS UK/Australia.

Commercial $3.9-4.1 billion, up 5%: LEAP-1A/787 MRO up 12%, A320neo/737 materials amid 38/month caps.

U.S. DoD 65% at $886 billion NDAA up 3%, our 2.1% share. International 22% vs prior 20%, F-35 Finland/Poland $600 million, Taiwan HIMARS.

Adjusted EPS $13.20-14.20, up 5% midpoint, margins 11.4-11.9% up 30 bps: Defense 12.8% Q2, Space 10.5%, Commercial 9.5%. FAS/CAS $0.15 headwind offset by $0.40 productivity/ASC 606.

Free cash flow $2.8-3.2 billion or 10% revenue: advances/progress payments, working capital 8%, capex $950 million hypersonics/F-35 ALIS.

Risks: titanium +18% Ukraine, Oklahoma labor 1-2% H2 pressure. Upside FY25 supplementals $60B+ Ukraine/Israel, China gray-zone AUKUS/QUAD. MBSE cut F-35 cycles 25%, $500 million friendshoring rare earths.

Embeds 8-10% organic growth, 1.15x book-to-bill. Dividend up 7% to $1.28/share, $1.5 billion buybacks.

Specific highlights: Gross margin 12.6%, operating income strong on mix, free cash flow $450 million Q3.

On free cash flow deeper: Q3 $1.2 billion up 25% YoY, YTD $3.8 billion toward $4.7-5.1 billion. Ops cash $1.7 billion from F-35 Lots 15/16 (120+ aircraft), hypersonics milestones. Cycle 45 days, DIO -8 via vendor programs, DSO 38.

Capex $500 million: 60% Fort Worth F-35 to 156/year, Huntsville hypersonics. FCF margin 12.5% > peers.

U.S. DoD 72%, FY24 NDAA $886 billion up 4.5%; FMS 22% HIMARS Poland/Australia; Middle East 6% MQ-9.

Utilization: 65% returns—$1.1 billion dividends 55% payout 2.1% yield, $1.2 billion buybacks 2.8% shares at $285, +4-5% 2025 EPS, ROIC >15%.

Delever 1.8x EBITDA from 2.3x, prepaid $600 million, green bond. Investments $800 million: $300 million digital thread SDA, $500 million M&A counter-UAS.

Offsets titanium/composites +12%, 85% hedged, nearshoring Mexico. FCF 8-10% CAGR to 2028, 5% sales growth $950 billion backlog.

Geopolitics shaping spend: SIPRI 2023 $2.44 trillion up 6.8%, 4-5% CAGR. U.S. $916 billion 37%, NATO €2 trillion decade. Book-to-bill 1.4x Q2, funded backlog $128 billion +12% YoY, RPO $185 billion.

Ukraine $175 billion U.S. supplementals $61 billion, JASSM/LRASM +35% production, Europe 22% revenue H1 $4.2 billion EMEA 28%.

Middle East $14.5 billion aid, Iron Dome/Arrow +40%, Patriot Saudi/UAE, GCC 8-10% GDP.

Indo-Pacific China DF-17/21D 500 by 2025, PDI $9.1 billion, AUKUS hypersonics $15-20 billion, Australia $368 billion, Japan GCAP $2.8 billion awards, QUAD JADC2 AI fusion +15-20% margins.

NGAD/NGAS CCA 60-70% fleets, hypersonics $180 billion market, ARRW scramjet/Mayhem LRIP, $450 million R&D STSS.

Risks CR delays $50-60 billion FY25, China FC-31, but $895 billion NDAA 3-4% growth.

FY24 high end $32-33 billion, defense margins 12.5% +150 bps.

Gross margin 12.6%, operating income robust, free cash flow on track.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, John. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 Lot 17 to 156 aircraft and hypersonics to 110% capacity. We are investing in automation, digital technologies, and model-based systems engineering to boost efficiency and cut costs 15-25% on design cycles. Titanium dual-sourcing U.S./Japan, nearshoring 70% critical tiers, ML forecasting contain inflation +3.2%.

Backlog details reinforce: Aeronautics 42% $74.9 billion +23% YoY F-35 $45 billion funded, NGAD 1.35x book-to-bill. Missiles $52.6 billion +18% ARRW/HACM $4.2 billion, Patriot GEM-T $1.8 billion, PACOM +35%, CENTCOM +22%. Space $28.7 billion +13% GPS/Vulcan $2.1 billion, LEO $900 million. Rotary $22 billion +10% CH-53K/MH-60R India $1.2 billion. U.S. 72% $128.3 billion +20%, int'l +25% APAC +32%, Europe +28%, Saudi THAAD $1.5 billion. Overall 1.28x book-to-bill, funded $92.4 billion 3.2 years, unfunded $85.8 billion incl $20 billion NGVC. FY24 to $190 billion B-21/787.

Program updates: NGAD digital phase CDR crewed/CCA, XA-102 +15% SFC vs F135, LRIP 14 vehicles, FRP Q4 FY25, backlog $22.4 billion +$4.2 billion, JASDF/RAAF $1.8 billion FMS. F-35 156 Lot 17 +10%, Block 4C first-flight APG-85/AI EW +25% discrimination, YTD $3.7 billion revenue $15.9 billion backlog, int'l Israel/Poland/Switzerland 95% on-time, GCC FMS +22% $2.1 billion UAE. Hypersonics ARRW/HACM test #5 B-52 Guam Mach 5+ ML nav, 28 rounds Q3 110-unit, $2.9 billion backlog Navy $850 million, unit cost -19% $14.2 million. Space Orion CV2 2025 lunar, ESM 100% tests Airbus +22%, 16/24 modules $1.2 billion YTD $8.6 billion backlog. Golden Dome 42 MEO sats 99.7% PNT anti-jam, +120 options $3.1 billion 14% margins Indo-Pac USSF. MQ-9B 18 Q3 +25% UK/India $1.4 billion, MQ-Next MUM-T Army FVL. Q3 segment revenue +9% $7.2 billion 1.3x book-to-bill. FY25 backlog $145-155 billion, export CAGR 15%.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Maria. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion like XA-102 adaptive cycle and scramjet for hypersonics, alongside AI/ML sensor fusion, digital twins, quantum-secure comms, and additive manufacturing reducing lead times 40%. MBSE accelerates NGAD/F-35 ODIN 25% faster bids B-21. Predictive analytics 98% accuracy, autonomy UAS MUM-T, resilient C4ISR JADC2, space anti-jam PNT, eVTOL fuel cells FAA 2026. $500 million five-year digital/quantum with Palantir AI sustainment. Partnerships GE, Raytheon, Northrop, Airbus, SpaceX ULA. These give competitive edge vs Raytheon, Northrop, Boeing in peer threats.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Sullivan with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Sullivan:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth and its breakdown by segment and region?

Alex Rivera:
Certainly, Mike. Our total backlog reached $178.2 billion, up $26.8 billion or 18% YoY and $12.4 billion or 7.5% QoQ, eighth consecutive double-digit quarter. Aeronautics 42% at $74.9 billion +23% on F-35 Lot 17 $8.1 billion and NGAD $2.3 billion. Missiles $52.6 billion +18% hypersonics $4.2 billion, PACOM +35% AUKUS, CENTCOM +22%. Space $28.7 +13% GPS/Vulcan/LEO. Rotary $22 +10% helicopters. U.S. DoD 72% $128.3 billion +20% NDAA/supplementals, international +25% $35.4 billion APAC +32% F-35 SK/Australia, Europe +28% F-16/Denmark, Saudi $1.5 billion. Funded $92.4 billion 52% 3.2 years visibility, 1.28x book-to-bill up from 1.15x.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the updated full-year guidance, particularly drivers and risks?

John Ramirez:
Lisa, great question. Raised revenue to $29.2-30.2 billion +4% midpoint, Defense $18.8-19.5 billion +6% F-35/JASSM/hypersonics, Space flat visible, Commercial +5% MRO. EPS $13.20-14.20 +5%, margins 11.4-11.9% +30 bps. FCF $2.8-3.2 billion 10%. Risks titanium/labor, but upside supplementals AUKUS, MBSE/friendshoring derisk.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Bradley with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Bradley:
Regarding the updates on key programs like NGAD and hypersonics?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Tom, happy to elaborate. NGAD CDR fighter/CCA XA-102 +15% SFC, LRIP 14 vehicles $22.4 billion backlog. F-35 Lot 17 156 Block 4C certified +25% targets $15.9 billion. ARRW/HACM test #5 success 28 rounds $2.9 billion. Orion ESM complete, Golden Dome 42 sats $3.1 billion. MQ-9B 18 units $1.4 billion. Execution strong 1.3x book-to-bill.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation across hypersonics, NGAD, space resilience, and commercial recovery, backed by $178 billion backlog and robust FCF.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay and transcript will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
